candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall handle and dispose of sewage sludge in accordance with Section 405 of the Clean Water Act and all other applicable Federal regulations to protect public health and the environment from any reasonably anticipated adverse effects due to any toxic pollutants which may be present.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether Section 405 and incorporated federal regulations supply enforceable numeric pollutant limits or monitoring duties for a facility determines which limits Purpose A compares against measurements and which monitoring obligations Purpose B treats as applicable.

candidates.exact_span: If requirements for sludge management practices or pollutant criteria become more stringent than the sludge pollutant limits or acceptable management practices in this permit, or control a pollutant not listed in this permit, this permit may be modified or revoked and reissued to conform to the requirements promulgated at Section 405(d)( 2) of the Clean Water Act.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of when external Section 405(d)(2) criteria supersede in-permit pollutant limits or management practices changes which numeric limits Purpose A applies and whether additional parameters or monitoring become applicable under Purpose B.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall give prior notice to EPA (Chief, Permits Branch, Water Management Division, Mail Code 6WQ -P, EPA Region 6, 1445 Ross Avenue, Dallas, Texas 75202) of any planned changes in the sewage sludge disposal practice, in accordance with 40 CFR Part 122.41(l)(1)(iii). These changes may justify the application of permit conditions that are different from or absent in the existing permit. Change in the sludge use or disposal practice may because for modification of the permit in accordance with 40 CFR Part 122.62(a)(1).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a disposal-practice change occurred and triggered notice or permit modification affects which permit conditions—and therefore which limits and monitoring requirements—are in force for FY2025 under Purposes A and B, and whether missing data reflects a documented practice change under Purpose C.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee or owner/operator shall submit a written closure and post closure plan to the permitting authority 180 days prior to the closure date.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a facility was within 180 days of closure in FY2025 establishes whether this submission obligation was applicable for that monitoring/reporting period.

candidates.exact_span: A discussion of how the leachate collection system will be operated and maintained for three years after the surface disposal site closes if it has a liner and leachate collection system.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the site has a liner and leachate collection system, and whether it had closed, determines if post-closure leachate operation obligations—and any associated monitoring or reporting—apply during FY2025 under Purposes B and C.

candidates.exact_span: A description of the system used to monitor continuously for methane gas in the air in any structures within the surface disposal site. The methane gas concentration shall not exceed 25% of the lower explosive limit for methane gas for three years after the sewage sludge unit closes.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a continuous methane monitoring obligation and an enforceable numeric concentration ceiling (25% LEL); different readings of site/structure scope, closure timing, or LEL basis change Purpose A exceedance determinations and Purpose B monitoring applicability.

candidates.exact_span: A description of the system used to monitor for methane gas in the air at the property line of the site shall be included. The methane gas concentration at the surface disposal site property line shall not exceed the lower explosive limit for methane gas for three years after the sewage sludge unit closes.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes property-line methane monitoring and a numeric limit at 100% LEL for three post-closure years; interpretation of property-line location, monitoring frequency, closure date, or LEL value changes applicable limits for Purpose A and required monitoring for Purpose B.

candidates.exact_span: A discussion of how public access to the surface disposal site will be restricted for three years after it closes.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a unit had closed within the prior three years determines if this post-closure obligation was active in FY2025 and whether absent access-restriction documentation reflects a documented no-data state or unresolved compliance evidence.

candidates.exact_span: An active sewage sludge unit located within 60 meters of a fault that has displacement in Holocene time shall close by March 22, 1994.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a unit is still treated as 'active' versus subject to mandatory closure affects which surface-disposal management and monitoring provisions apply in FY2025 under Purposes B and C, and whether methane or other post-closure limits govern.

candidates.exact_span: An active sewage sludge unit located in an unstable area shall close by March 22, 1994.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Classification of a site as an 'unstable area' and whether the unit remains 'active' changes which ongoing management and monitoring requirements are treated as applicable versus superseded by closure obligations.

candidates.exact_span: An active sewage sludge unit located in a wetland shall close by March 22, 1994.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Wetland location and active-unit status affect whether FY2025 obligations are evaluated under active-unit management practices or post-closure methane and access restrictions, changing monitoring and limit applicability under Purposes B and C.

candidates.exact_span: Surface disposal shall not restrict the flow of the base 100-year flood.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Although not a concentration limit, interpretation of 'restrict the flow' and the applicable base 100-year flood standard determines whether this enforceable performance criterion is an applicable limit for comparison when hydraulic evidence is reported.

candidates.exact_span: The run-off collection system for an active sewage sludge unit shall have the capacity to handle run-off from a 25-year, 24-hour storm event.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a unit qualifies as 'active' and whether reported runoff or storm-event data satisfy the 25-year/24-hour design standard affects enforceable compliance evaluation under Purpose A and whether storm-related monitoring or demonstration was required under Purpose B.

candidates.exact_span: A food crop, feed crop, or a fiber crop shall not be grown on a surface disposal site.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Determining whether crop-growth prohibition monitoring or inspection was required for a surface disposal site in FY2025 depends on how 'surface disposal site' is scoped and whether crop activity triggers reporting obligations.
